A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same response-planning study. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices A–B support reliable comparison despite figure renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original probing results across six response attributes, cross-dataset evaluations, and ablations in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds character-choice self-estimation results in Section 5.3 and Figure 8b.

M1.justification: The hidden-representation probing procedure, MLP architecture, losses, and greedy-decoded attribute targets are retained. The new schematic and shortcut discussion explain existing procedures; planning-aware training is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: The same six attribute tasks and twelve prompt datasets are retained. The added self-estimation comparison uses TinyStories character-choice prediction, which was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Section 5.3 adds explicitly prompted self-estimation as a comparator for character-choice probing on TinyStories. In v1, this comparator was evaluated only for response length on Ultrachat; the other comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: v2 extends separate-run self-estimation evaluation to character identity, comparing estimates with greedy-decoded choices using F1 in Figure 8b. Existing probe splits, training budgets, hyperparameter searches, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The analysis of the gap between probed information and verbalized self-predictions expands from response length to character choice. Existing sensitivity, layer, scaling, and generation-position analyses are retained. Section 6.2 adds discussion rather than a new shortcut-control experiment.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 7 adds shaded bands around generation-position performance curves that appeared without bands in v1 Figure 6. Their statistical meaning is unspecified. Both versions retain three-seed averaging, with no documented increase in runs.

E6.justification: Figure 8b adds character-choice self-estimation and corresponding probing scores for eight models; for example, Qwen2-7B has F1 scores of 0.10 and 0.86, respectively. The earlier response-length comparison and Appendix B regression results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and probing formulation in Sections 3.1–3.2 are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or derivation. Section 6.2 elaborates the existing requirement that target attributes cannot be determined from the first response token.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the 'fine-tuned' qualifier from its model-size scaling claim, slightly broadening the stated scope although Section 5.1 still evaluates tuned models. The central response-planning, attribute-encoding, and potential controllability contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 6.2 explains first-token shortcut correlations and argues that existing analysis-before-answer prompts mitigate them. The discussion also expands potential generation control and planning-aware training applications, while retaining the unresolved causal and sampling limitations.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix A retain the same training details, prompt templates, labeling, filtering, augmentation, representation collection, and model/dataset access information. The added character self-estimation comparison does not supply its exact prompt or additional implementation details.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work positioning, and claim to the first formal response-planning framework are retained. Editorial and publication-header updates do not change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 pluralizes the title, standardizes terminology, edits author information and contributions, rewrites Section 5.3, and expands the discussion with a new subsection and enumerated future directions. Most methodological and results prose retains its original structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds a front-page explanatory schematic and substantially redesigns the layer heatmaps with model labels, layer indices, color scales, and overlaid relative-performance curves. It also redesigns the generation plots and expands the self-estimation display into two panels, beyond simple renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The labeled layer plots and new schematic improve interpretability, while the character-choice comparison strengthens the evidence for the probing–self-estimation gap. The shortcut discussion clarifies the intended controls but adds no validating control experiment, and the new shaded bands remain undefined. These support a limited overall improvement.
